title.zh: 簡單過去式：講完成了的事
title.en: The preterite: things that got done

intro.zh:
簡單過去式（pretérito indefinido）用來講**已經結束**的動作 —— 有明確的起點或終點，事情發生完了。

規則變化只有兩組字尾：-ar 一組，-er 和 -ir 共用另一組。

**yo 和 él 那兩格都有重音符號**，而且重音落在最後一個音節。這是初學階段最常漏的細節，漏掉會直接變成別的時態。
intro.en:
The preterite (pretérito indefinido) is for actions that are **finished** — with a clear start or end, and done with.

Regular verbs use just two sets of endings: one for -ar, and one shared by -er and -ir.

**The yo and él forms both carry a written accent**, with the stress on the final syllable. That accent is the detail most often dropped at this level, and dropping it turns the word into a different tense.

rule.zh: **-ar 動詞**：-é / -aste / -ó / -amos / -aron。
rule.en: **-ar verbs**: -é / -aste / -ó / -amos / -aron.

gloss.zh: 我昨天跟我姐姐講過話。
gloss.en: Yesterday I spoke with my sister.

examples.es: Ella viajó a Cuenca en bus.

gloss.en: She travelled to Cuenca by bus.

rule.zh: **-er 與 -ir 動詞**共用：-í / -iste / -ió / -imos / -ieron。
rule.en: **-er and -ir verbs** share one set: -í / -iste / -ió / -imos / -ieron.

examples.es: Comí en un restaurante del centro.

gloss.zh: 我在市中心一家餐廳吃了飯。
gloss.en: I ate at a restaurant downtown.

examples.es: El bus salió a las ocho.

gloss.en: We lived there for two years.

rule.zh: **yo 和 él 那兩格一定有重音符號**，而且重音在最後一個音節。
rule.en: **The yo and él forms always carry a written accent**, with the stress on the last syllable.

gloss.zh: 我說（現在）→ 我說了（過去）

note.zh: 沒有重音符號就變回現在式
note.en: Without the accent it reverts to the present tense.

gloss.zh: 他說（現在）→ 他說了（過去）

rule.zh: 搭配**明確的過去時間詞**最自然：ayer、anoche、el año pasado、hace dos horas。
rule.en: It pairs naturally with **a definite past time expression**: ayer, anoche, el año pasado, hace dos horas.

gloss.en: Last night I got in very late.

examples.es: El año pasado viajamos a Galápagos.

gloss.zh: 去年我們去了加拉巴哥。
gloss.en: Last year we travelled to the Galápagos.

rule.zh: **-ar 和 -ir 的 nosotros 跟現在式同形**，靠時間詞或上下文分辨。
rule.en: **The nosotros form of -ar and -ir verbs is identical to the present**; time expressions or context tell them apart.

gloss.zh: 我們說西班牙文。／我們（那時）說了西班牙文。
gloss.en: We speak Spanish. / We spoke Spanish.

gloss.zh: 我們昨天跟導遊講過話。
gloss.en: Yesterday we spoke with the guide.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**漏掉重音符號**：

- ✗ Ayer yo hablo con ella. → ✓ Ayer yo **hablé** con ella.
- ✗ Ella viajo a Cuenca. → ✓ Ella **viajó** a Cuenca.

> 自我檢查：hablo 和 habló 是兩個不同時態的字。前者是「我現在說」，後者是「他說了」。重音符號不是裝飾，它就是時態本身。

第二個是**把 -er 和 -ir 的字尾用成 -ar 的**：

- ✗ Yo comé. → ✓ Yo **comí**.
- ✗ Ellos vivaron. → ✓ Ellos **vivieron**.

-ar 用 a 系列，-er／-ir 用 i 系列，兩組不能混。

第三個是**在 nosotros 那格自己加重音**：

- ✗ hablámos → ✓ **hablamos**

只有 yo 和 él 兩格有重音符號，nosotros 沒有。

> 記憶策略：把兩組字尾各背成一串節奏 —— é-aste-ó-amos-aron 和 í-iste-ió-imos-ieron。頭尾兩個字尾是辨識關鍵，中間三個很好記。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **dropping the written accent**:

- ✗ Ayer yo hablo con ella. → ✓ Ayer yo **hablé** con ella.
- ✗ Ella viajo a Cuenca. → ✓ Ella **viajó** a Cuenca.

> Self-check: hablo and habló are two different tenses. One is “I speak now”, the other “he spoke”. The accent isn’t decoration — it *is* the tense.

Second, **using -ar endings on -er/-ir verbs**:

- ✗ Yo comé. → ✓ Yo **comí**.
- ✗ Ellos vivaron. → ✓ Ellos **vivieron**.

-ar takes the a-series, -er/-ir take the i-series; the two never mix.

Third, **adding an accent to the nosotros form**:

- ✗ hablámos → ✓ **hablamos**

Only yo and él carry a written accent; nosotros doesn’t.

> A strategy: learn each set as a rhythm — é-aste-ó-amos-aron and í-iste-ió-imos-ieron. The first and last endings do the identifying work; the middle three are easy.

explain.zh: -ar 動詞的 yo 是 -é，一定要有重音符號。
explain.en: The yo ending for -ar verbs is -é, and the accent is required.

explain.zh: -ar 動詞的 él 是 -ó。
explain.en: The él ending for -ar verbs is -ó.

explain.zh: -er 動詞的 yo 是 -í：com- + í。
explain.en: The yo ending for -er verbs is -í: com- + í.

explain.zh: -ir 動詞的 ellos 是 -ieron。
explain.en: The ellos ending for -ir verbs is -ieron.

explain.zh: salir 的簡單過去式是規則的：sal- + ió。
explain.en: The preterite of salir is regular: sal- + ió.

explain.zh: hablo 是現在式，habló 是過去式。重音符號決定時態。
explain.en: hablo is present, habló is past. The written accent decides the tense.

explain.en: viajé is stressed on the final syllable and carries a written accent — that is how the yo slot of the preterite always looks. ayer frames the time, which is the most natural companion for this tense.

exercises.es: Ayer viajé a Cuenca en bus.

gloss.zh: 我昨天搭公車去了昆卡。
gloss.en: Yesterday I travelled to Cuenca by bus.

explain.en: The nosotros form of -ar verbs is the same in the present and the preterite; time expressions disambiguate.

prompt.en: What tense is hablamos in “Ayer hablamos con el guía”?

optionExplains.en: Correct: the time expression removes the ambiguity.

explain.en: The yo form of llegar is llegué — -gar verbs insert a u before -é to keep the sound.

prompt.zh: 把「我兩小時前到的。」翻成西班牙文

explain.zh: -ar 動詞的 ellos 是 -aron。
explain.en: The ellos ending for -ar verbs is -aron.

title.zh: 簡單過去式：不規則的那一群

intro.zh:
最常用的動詞在簡單過去式裡幾乎都是不規則的。好消息是它們**共用同一組字尾**，而且那組字尾**完全沒有重音符號**。

字尾：**-e / -iste / -o / -imos / -ieron**

要背的是每個動詞的**新字根**。字根換掉之後，字尾一律照上面那組接。

ser 和 ir 兩個動詞在這個時態**長得一模一樣**，靠上下文分辨。
intro.en:
The most-used verbs are nearly all irregular in the preterite. The good news: they **share one set of endings**, and that set carries **no written accents at all**.

Endings: **-e / -iste / -o / -imos / -ieron**

What you memorise is each verb’s **new stem**. Once the stem is swapped in, the endings above go on unchanged.

ser and ir are **identical** in this tense; context tells them apart.

rule.zh: 這一組的字尾**完全沒有重音符號** —— 跟規則變化最大的差別。
rule.en: This group’s endings carry **no written accents** — the biggest difference from the regular pattern.

examples.es: tener → tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvieron

note.zh: tuve 和 tuvo 都沒有重音符號
note.en: Neither tuve nor tuvo takes an accent.

examples.es: Ella tuvo un problema con el vuelo.

gloss.en: She had a problem with her flight.

rule.zh: **字根是 u 的一群**：tener → tuv-、estar → estuv-、poder → pud-、poner → pus-、saber → sup-。
rule.en: **The u-stem group**: tener → tuv-, estar → estuv-, poder → pud-, poner → pus-, saber → sup-.

gloss.en: We were in Cuenca for three days.

examples.es: Puso el equipaje en el carro.

gloss.en: He put the luggage in the car.
I found out the news last night.

rule.zh: **字根是 i 的一群**：hacer → hic-、querer → quis-、venir → vin-。hacer 的 él 那格會變成 **hizo**。
rule.en: **The i-stem group**: hacer → hic-, querer → quis-, venir → vin-. The él form of hacer becomes **hizo**.

note.zh: c 變成 z 才能保住發音
note.en: The c becomes z to keep the sound.

rule.zh: **字根帶 j 的一群**：decir → dij-、traer → traj-。這群的 ellos 用 **-eron**，不是 -ieron。
rule.en: **The j-stem group**: decir → dij-, traer → traj-. Their ellos ending is **-eron**, not -ieron.

gloss.en: He told me it was closed.

rule.zh: **ser 和 ir 在這個時態同形**：fui / fuiste / fue / fuimos / fueron。
rule.en: **ser and ir are identical here**: fui / fuiste / fue / fuimos / fueron.

gloss.en: I went to Cuenca by bus.
It was a very long trip.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**在不規則形式上加重音符號**：

- ✗ tuvé → ✓ **tuve**
- ✗ estuvó → ✓ **estuvo**
- ✗ hicé → ✓ **hice**

> 自我檢查：這一組的字尾是 -e / -iste / -o / -imos / -ieron，一個重音符號都沒有。看到不規則字根還配著重音符號，就是錯的。

第二個是**把規則字尾套到不規則字根上**：

- ✗ Yo tení → ✓ Yo **tuve**
- ✗ Yo hací → ✓ Yo **hice**

字根換了，字尾也要跟著換成這一組。

第三個是 **j 字根那群的 ellos 多了一個 i**：

- ✗ dijieron → ✓ **dijeron**
- ✗ trajieron → ✓ **trajeron**

字根結尾是 j 的時候，-ieron 的 i 會被吃掉。

第四個是 **hacer 的 él 忘了換字母**：

- ✗ hico → ✓ **hizo**

c 在 o 前面會唸成 /k/，跟 hacer 的音對不上，所以改寫成 z。

> 記憶策略：這些動詞的簡單過去式沒有規律可推，但數量有限。把「新字根」單獨記起來（tuv、estuv、pud、pus、sup、hic、quis、vin、dij），字尾那一串是共用的，記一次就夠。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **putting accents on the irregular forms**:

- ✗ tuvé → ✓ **tuve**
- ✗ estuvó → ✓ **estuvo**
- ✗ hicé → ✓ **hice**

> Self-check: this group’s endings are -e / -iste / -o / -imos / -ieron, with no accent anywhere. An irregular stem carrying a written accent is wrong.

Second, **putting regular endings on an irregular stem**:

- ✗ Yo tení → ✓ Yo **tuve**
- ✗ Yo hací → ✓ Yo **hice**

When the stem changes, the endings change with it.

Third, **an extra i in the j-stem ellos form**:

- ✗ dijieron → ✓ **dijeron**
- ✗ trajieron → ✓ **trajeron**

When the stem ends in j, the i of -ieron is absorbed.

Fourth, **forgetting the letter swap in hacer’s él form**:

- ✗ hico → ✓ **hizo**

Before o, a c would be pronounced /k/, which no longer matches hacer, so it is written z instead.

> A strategy: these preterites can’t be derived, but there aren’t many. Memorise just the new stems (tuv, estuv, pud, pus, sup, hic, quis, vin, dij); the ending string is shared, so you learn it once.

explain.en: The stem of tener becomes tuv-, and the -e ending has no accent.

explain.zh: estar 的字根是 estuv-。
explain.en: The stem of estar is estuv-.

explain.zh: hacer 的 él 是 hizo —— c 改寫成 z 才能保住發音。
explain.en: The él form of hacer is hizo — the c is written z to keep the sound.

explain.zh: decir 的字根帶 j，ellos 用 -eron 不是 -ieron。
explain.en: The stem of decir ends in j, so ellos takes -eron, not -ieron.

explain.zh: poder 的字根是 pud-。
explain.en: The stem of poder is pud-.

explain.zh: ir 與 ser 在這個時態同形，yo 都是 fui。
explain.en: ir and ser are identical here; the yo form of both is fui.

explain.zh: tuve 沒有重音符號，重音落在第一個音節 —— 不規則那一群的字尾一律不帶重音符號，這是跟規則變化最好認的差別。tener que + 不定式是「必須」。
explain.en: tuve carries no written accent and is stressed on the first syllable — none of the irregular group takes an accent on its endings, which is the easiest way to tell them from the regular ones. tener que + infinitive means “to have to”.

explain.zh: 字根結尾是 j 時，-ieron 的 i 會被吃掉。
explain.en: When the stem ends in j, the i of -ieron is absorbed.

optionExplains.en: A j-stem doesn’t take -ieron.

prompt.en: Translate into Spanish: “I went to Cuenca by bus.”

title.zh: 未完成過去式：過去的背景與習慣
title.en: The imperfect: past background and habits

intro.zh:
未完成過去式（imperfecto）講的是過去的**背景、習慣、持續狀態**，不強調事情有沒有結束。

這是西班牙文最好學的時態之一：字尾只有兩組，而且**只有三個動詞不規則** —— ser、ir、ver。

-ar 用 -aba 系列，-er 和 -ir 共用 -ía 系列。
intro.en:
The imperfect describes **background, habits and ongoing states** in the past, without saying whether anything finished.

It is one of the easiest Spanish tenses: two sets of endings, and **only three irregular verbs** — ser, ir and ver.

-ar verbs take the -aba series; -er and -ir share the -ía series.

rule.zh: **-ar 動詞**：-aba / -abas / -aba / -ábamos / -aban。
rule.en: **-ar verbs**: -aba / -abas / -aba / -ábamos / -aban.

examples.es: Cuando era niño, jugaba en el parque.

gloss.en: When I was a child, I used to play in the park.

examples.es: Mi abuela cocinaba todos los domingos.

gloss.zh: 我奶奶以前每個星期天做菜。
gloss.en: My grandmother used to cook every Sunday.
We walked a lot in those days.

rule.zh: **-er 與 -ir 動詞**共用：-ía / -ías / -ía / -íamos / -ían。
rule.en: **-er and -ir verbs** share: -ía / -ías / -ía / -íamos / -ían.

examples.es: Comíamos a la una todos los días.

gloss.zh: 我們以前每天一點吃飯。
gloss.en: We used to eat at one every day.
It was raining when we left.

rule.zh: 只有**三個動詞不規則**：ser、ir、ver。整個時態就這三個要背。
rule.en: Only **three verbs are irregular**: ser, ir, ver. That’s the whole list.

examples.es: ser → era, eras, era, éramos, eran
ir → iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban
ver → veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veían
Cuando era joven, iba al campo cada verano.

gloss.zh: 我年輕時每年夏天都去鄉下。
gloss.en: When I was young, I went to the countryside every summer.

rule.zh: 用來講**過去的習慣**，常搭配 siempre、todos los días、cada año、antes。
rule.en: It expresses **past habits**, often with siempre, todos los días, cada año, antes.

examples.es: Antes tomaba café todas las mañanas.

gloss.zh: 我以前每天早上喝咖啡。
gloss.en: I used to have coffee every morning.
He was always late to class.

examples.es: Cada año visitábamos a mis abuelos.

gloss.zh: 我們每年都去看祖父母。
gloss.en: Every year we visited my grandparents.

rule.zh: 也用來描述**過去的狀態與背景**：年齡、天氣、時間、心情、外表。
rule.en: It also describes **past states and background**: age, weather, time, mood, appearance.

gloss.en: I was twenty when I arrived.

examples.es: Eran las ocho de la noche.

gloss.en: It was eight in the evening.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**在 -ía 系列漏掉重音符號**：

- ✗ comia → ✓ **comía**
- ✗ vivia → ✓ **vivía**

> 自我檢查：-er／-ir 的未完成過去式**每一格都有重音符號**，五格全部都有，一格都不能漏。這跟簡單過去式只有兩格有重音符號正好相反。

第二個是 **-ar 的 nosotros 漏了重音符號**：

- ✗ hablabamos → ✓ **hablábamos**

-aba 系列只有 nosotros 這一格有重音符號，其餘四格沒有。

第三個是**把 ser 或 ir 當成規則動詞**：

- ✗ Yo sía → ✓ Yo **era**
- ✗ Yo ía → ✓ Yo **iba**

這個時態只有三個不規則動詞，剛好都是最常用的。

> 記憶策略：兩組字尾的重音符號位置正好相反 —— -aba 系列只有 nosotros 有，-ía 系列則是每一格都有。記住這個對比，重音就不會亂放。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **dropping the accent in the -ía series**:

- ✗ comia → ✓ **comía**
- ✗ vivia → ✓ **vivía**

> Self-check: for -er/-ir verbs the imperfect carries an accent in **every one of the five forms** — not a single one is bare. That’s the mirror image of the preterite, where only two forms take an accent.

Second, **missing the accent on the -ar nosotros form**:

- ✗ hablabamos → ✓ **hablábamos**

In the -aba series only nosotros takes an accent; the other four don’t.

Third, **treating ser or ir as regular**:

- ✗ Yo sía → ✓ Yo **era**
- ✗ Yo ía → ✓ Yo **iba**

This tense has only three irregular verbs, and they happen to be among the most used.

> A strategy: the two sets are accent mirror images — the -aba series accents only nosotros, the -ía series accents everything. Hold on to that contrast and the accents fall into place.

explain.zh: -ar 的未完成過去式 yo 是 -aba，沒有重音符號。
explain.en: The -ar imperfect yo ending is -aba, with no accent.

explain.zh: -ar 的 nosotros 是唯一有重音符號的一格：-ábamos。
explain.en: The -ar nosotros form is the only accented one: -ábamos.

explain.zh: -er 的未完成過去式每一格都有重音符號：comía。
explain.en: Every -er imperfect form carries an accent: comía.

explain.zh: ser 是三個不規則之一：era。
explain.en: ser is one of the three irregulars: era.

explain.zh: ir 的未完成過去式是 iba。
explain.en: The imperfect of ir is iba.

title.zh: 兩種過去式：哪一個講什麼
title.en: The two past tenses: which one does what

intro.zh:
西班牙文有兩個常用的過去時態，選哪一個**不是看事情發生多久**，而是看你想**怎麼講這件事**。

- **簡單過去式**：把事件當成一個完成的點 —— 發生了、結束了。
- **未完成過去式**：把事件當成一段背景 —— 那時的狀況、當時正在進行、以前的習慣。

同一件事可以用兩種時態講，聽起來的意思會不一樣。這一課的重點就是那個差別。
intro.en:
Spanish has two everyday past tenses, and the choice **isn’t about how long ago something happened** — it’s about **how you want to present it**.

- **Preterite**: the event as a completed point — it happened, it finished.
- **Imperfect**: the event as background — the situation at the time, something in progress, a former habit.

The same event can be told either way, and it means something different each time. That difference is what this lesson is about.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**用「多久以前」來決定時態**。時間遠近跟選哪個時態沒有關係：

- Ayer **llovía** cuando salí.（昨天，用未完成過去式，因為是背景）
- Hace diez años **fui** a Cuenca.（十年前，用簡單過去式，因為是完成的事件）

> 自我檢查：問自己「我是在講**發生了什麼事**，還是在講**當時是什麼狀況**？」前者用簡單過去式，後者用未完成過去式。

第二個是**把背景也講成事件**：

- ✗ Cuando salí, llovió.（意思變成「我出門，然後下了一場雨」）
- ✓ Cuando salí, **llovía**.（我出門時外面正在下雨）

兩句都合文法，但意思不同。要講背景就得用未完成過去式。

第三個是**期間明確卻用了未完成過去式**：

- ✗ Viví... 不對，✗ Vivía en Quito dos años. → ✓ **Viví** en Quito dos años.

只要講出「兩年」「三次」這種有邊界的量，那段時間就是關閉的，用簡單過去式。

第四個是**忽略換時態換意思的那幾個動詞**：

- **conocía** = 早就認識；**conocí** = 第一次認識（初次見面）
- **sabía** = 本來就知道；**supe** = 得知（那一刻才知道）
- **podía** = 那時有能力；**pude** = 設法做到了

> 記憶策略：想像在講一個故事。**背景像照片**（天氣、時間、心情、周圍的人在做什麼）用未完成過去式；**情節像影片裡的一個鏡頭**（然後發生了什麼）用簡單過去式。一段故事通常兩種都會用到。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **choosing the tense by how long ago something happened**. Distance in time has nothing to do with it:

- Ayer **llovía** cuando salí. (yesterday, imperfect, because it’s background)
- Hace diez años **fui** a Cuenca. (ten years ago, preterite, because it’s a completed event)

> Self-check: ask yourself “am I saying **what happened**, or **what things were like**?” The first takes the preterite, the second the imperfect.

Second, **telling background as if it were an event**:

- ✗ Cuando salí, llovió. (this says “I went out, and then a rain shower happened”)
- ✓ Cuando salí, **llovía**. (it was raining as I went out)

Both are grammatical, but they mean different things. Background needs the imperfect.

Third, **using the imperfect with a stated span**:

- ✗ Vivía en Quito dos años. → ✓ **Viví** en Quito dos años.

As soon as you state a bounded amount — two years, three times — the span is closed, so it takes the preterite.

Fourth, **ignoring the verbs that change meaning**:

- **conocía** = already knew someone; **conocí** = met them for the first time
- **sabía** = already knew a fact; **supe** = found it out at that moment
- **podía** = was able to; **pude** = managed to

> A strategy: picture telling a story. **Background is a photograph** (weather, time, mood, what people around you were doing) — imperfect. **Plot is a shot in a film** (and then this happened) — preterite. Most stories need both.

intro.zh:
**haber + 過去分詞**，用來講「到目前為止」發生過的事 —— 時間範圍還沒關閉。

haber 的現在式：he / has / ha / hemos / han。過去分詞：-ar → **-ado**，-er／-ir → **-ido**。

兩個部分**不能拆開**，中間不能插字，而且過去分詞永遠不變形。

拉美日常口語裡，這個時態用得比西班牙少 —— 很多場合直接用簡單過去式就可以了。
intro.en:
**haber + past participle** reports what has happened **up to now** — the time frame is still open.

The present tense of haber: he / has / ha / hemos / han. Participles: -ar → **-ado**, -er/-ir → **-ido**.

The two parts **can’t be separated** — nothing goes between them — and the participle never changes form.

In everyday Latin American speech this tense is used less than in Spain; in many situations the plain preterite does the job.

rule.zh: **haber 變位 + 過去分詞**。兩個部分要連在一起。
rule.en: **Conjugated haber + past participle.** The two parts stay together.

rule.zh: 過去分詞：-ar → **-ado**，-er／-ir → **-ido**。**永遠不隨主詞變形**。
rule.en: Participles: -ar → **-ado**, -er/-ir → **-ido**. They **never change for the subject**.

rule.zh: **不規則分詞**要單獨背：hacer → hecho、decir → dicho、ver → visto、poner → puesto、volver → vuelto、abrir → abierto、escribir → escrito、morir → muerto、romper → roto。
rule.en: **Irregular participles** are memorised: hacer → hecho, decir → dicho, ver → visto, poner → puesto, volver → vuelto, abrir → abierto, escribir → escrito, morir → muerto, romper → roto.

rule.zh: 搭配**還沒關閉的時間範圍**：hoy、esta semana、este año、ya、todavía no、nunca、alguna vez。
rule.en: It pairs with **time frames that are still open**: hoy, esta semana, este año, ya, todavía no, nunca, alguna vez.

rule.zh: 代名詞放在 **haber 前面**，不能插進 haber 和分詞中間。
rule.en: Pronouns go **before haber**, never between haber and the participle.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**讓過去分詞跟著主詞變形**：

- ✗ Ellas han hablada. → ✓ Ellas han **hablado**.
- ✗ Nosotros hemos comidos. → ✓ Nosotros hemos **comido**.

> 自我檢查：過去分詞在這個結構裡永遠是同一個形狀，不管主詞是誰、幾個人、什麼性別。

第二個是**把兩個部分拆開**：

- ✗ He no comido. → ✓ **No he** comido.
- ✗ He lo visto. → ✓ **Lo he** visto.

否定詞和代名詞都放在 haber 前面，不能插進中間。

第三個是**用 tener 代替 haber**：

- ✗ Tengo comido. → ✓ **He** comido.

tener 是「擁有」，這個結構只能用 haber。

第四個是**不規則分詞用規則形式硬套**：

- ✗ he hacido → ✓ he **hecho**
- ✗ he vido → ✓ he **visto**
- ✗ he escribido → ✓ he **escrito**

> 拉美用法提醒：在厄瓜多的日常對話裡，很多情況會直接用簡單過去式 —— ¿Ya comiste? 跟 ¿Ya has comido? 都聽得到，前者更常見。這個時態要會聽會用，但不必勉強自己每次都用它。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **making the participle agree with the subject**:

- ✗ Ellas han hablada. → ✓ Ellas han **hablado**.
- ✗ Nosotros hemos comidos. → ✓ Nosotros hemos **comido**.

> Self-check: in this structure the participle keeps one shape regardless of who the subject is, how many, or which gender.

Second, **splitting the two parts**:

- ✗ He no comido. → ✓ **No he** comido.
- ✗ He lo visto. → ✓ **Lo he** visto.

Negatives and pronouns both go before haber; nothing gets inserted in the middle.

Third, **using tener instead of haber**:

- ✗ Tengo comido. → ✓ **He** comido.

tener means “to own”; only haber builds this structure.

Fourth, **forcing regular endings onto irregular participles**:

- ✗ he hacido → ✓ he **hecho**
- ✗ he vido → ✓ he **visto**
- ✗ he escribido → ✓ he **escrito**

> A note on Latin American usage: in everyday Ecuadorian conversation the plain preterite often does this job — you’ll hear both ¿Ya comiste? and ¿Ya has comido?, with the first being more common. Learn to recognise and use this tense, but don’t force it into every sentence.

explain.en: A conjugated haber (han) plus a participle (hablado), with nothing allowed in between. The participle is always -ado/-ido and never agrees with the subject — it does not become habladas here.

title.en: The future tense: predictions and guesses

intro.zh:
未來式的作法很特別：字尾直接接在**完整的不定式**後面，不用切掉字尾。

字尾只有一組，三類動詞共用：**-é / -ás / -á / -emos / -án**。除了 nosotros 之外每一格都有重音符號。

日常講計畫還是 ir a + 原形更常用；未來式多半用在**預測**、**承諾**，以及一個很實用的用法 —— **推測現在的事**。
intro.en:
The future tense is built unusually: the endings attach to the **whole infinitive**, with nothing chopped off.

There is only one set of endings, shared by all three verb classes: **-é / -ás / -á / -emos / -án**. Every form except nosotros carries a written accent.

For everyday plans, ir a + infinitive is still more common. The future tense is mostly used for **predictions**, **promises**, and one very practical job — **guessing about the present**.

rule.zh: 字尾接在**完整的不定式**後面，三類動詞共用一組。
rule.en: The endings attach to the **complete infinitive**, and all three classes share one set.

rule.zh: **只有 nosotros 沒有重音符號**，其餘四格都有。
rule.en: **Only nosotros lacks a written accent**; the other four all have one.

note.zh: nosotros 是唯一沒有重音符號的
note.en: nosotros is the only one without an accent.

rule.zh: **十二個動詞的字根會縮短或改變**，字尾仍然是同一組。
rule.en: Twelve verbs **shorten or alter their stem**, but the endings stay the same.

rule.zh: 用來講**預測**與**承諾**。
rule.en: Used for **predictions** and **promises**.

gloss.en: It will rain in the highlands tomorrow.
The project will finish in March.

rule.zh: 很實用的第二種用法：**推測現在的事**，相當於「大概、應該是」。
rule.en: A very useful second job: **guessing about the present**, the equivalent of “probably” or “it must be”.

gloss.en: I wonder what time it is.

note.en: This is about now, not the future.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**把不定式的字尾切掉**：

- ✗ hablé（這是簡單過去式）→ ✓ **hablaré**
- ✗ comeré 對；但 ✗ comé 不是未來式

> 自我檢查：未來式的形狀是「完整不定式 + 字尾」。hablar 還在裡面，才是未來式。

第二個是**跟簡單過去式的 yo 搞混**：

- **hablé** = 我說了（過去）
- **hablaré** = 我會說（未來）

差別只有中間那個 ar，但意思完全相反。

第三個是**在 nosotros 加了重音符號**：

- ✗ hablarémos → ✓ **hablaremos**

這是唯一沒有重音符號的一格。

第四個是**把不規則字根用回原形**：

- ✗ teneré → ✓ **tendré**
- ✗ haceré → ✓ **haré**

這十二個動詞的字根縮短了，但字尾照舊。

> 實務提醒：日常講計畫時，ir a + 原形（Voy a viajar）比未來式自然得多。未來式在口語裡最常出現的其實是**推測**用法 —— ¿Dónde estará mi celular?（我手機到底在哪？）
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **chopping the infinitive ending off**:

- ✗ hablé (that’s the preterite) → ✓ **hablaré**
- comeré is right; comé is not a future form

> Self-check: a future form is “whole infinitive + ending”. If hablar is still in there, it’s the future.

Second, **confusing it with the preterite yo form**:

- **hablé** = I spoke (past)
- **hablaré** = I will speak (future)

One syllable apart, opposite meanings.

Third, **adding an accent to nosotros**:

- ✗ hablarémos → ✓ **hablaremos**

That’s the one form without an accent.

Fourth, **restoring the full stem on the irregular twelve**:

- ✗ teneré → ✓ **tendré**
- ✗ haceré → ✓ **haré**

Their stems are shortened, but the endings are unchanged.

> A practical note: for everyday plans, ir a + infinitive (Voy a viajar) sounds far more natural than the future tense. What you’ll actually hear the future used for in speech is **guessing** — ¿Dónde estará mi celular? (Where on earth is my phone?)

title.zh: 條件式：客氣的說法與假設

intro.zh:
條件式跟未來式**共用同一個字根**（完整的不定式，或同樣那十二個縮短字根），只是換一組字尾：

**-ía / -ías / -ía / -íamos / -ían**

這組字尾**每一格都有重音符號**。

最實用的用途是**把話說得客氣** —— 在餐廳、商店、問路的時候，用條件式比用現在式柔和得多。
intro.en:
The conditional **shares its stem with the future** (the whole infinitive, or those same twelve shortened stems); only the endings change:

**-ía / -ías / -ía / -íamos / -ían**

Every one of these endings carries a written accent.

Its most useful job is **softening what you say** — in a restaurant, a shop, or when asking directions, the conditional sounds considerably gentler than the present.

rule.zh: 字根跟未來式完全一樣，只換字尾。**每一格都有重音符號**。
rule.en: Same stem as the future, different endings. **Every form has a written accent.**

note.zh: 未來式是 tendré，字根相同
note.en: The future is tendré — same stem.

rule.zh: **最實用的用途：把請求說得客氣。**
rule.en: **The most useful job: making a request polite.**

rule.en: Used for **hypotheticals** — how things would be if circumstances differed.

gloss.en: It would be better to take a taxi.
I’d like to visit the Galápagos.

rule.en: Used for **the future seen from the past** — what was going to happen, viewed from back then.

gloss.en: He said he would arrive at eight.
I thought it would be easier.

rule.zh: 也可以**推測過去的事**，跟未來式推測現在是同一種用法。
rule.en: It can also **guess about the past**, mirroring how the future guesses about the present.

gloss.en: What time would it have been when you arrived?
It must have been about ten.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**漏掉重音符號**：

- ✗ podria → ✓ **podría**
- ✗ gustaria → ✓ **gustaría**

> 自我檢查：條件式的五格**全部**都有重音符號，一格都不能漏。這跟未來式（只有 nosotros 沒有）正好相反。

第二個是**跟未完成過去式的 -ía 混淆**：

- **comía** = 我那時在吃（未完成過去式，字根是 com-）
- **comería** = 我會吃（條件式，字根是完整的 comer）

差別在字根：條件式保留完整的不定式，未完成過去式把字尾切掉了。

第三個是**該客氣的時候用了現在式**。文法上沒錯，但語氣差很多：

- Quiero una habitación.（我要一間房）—— 直接
- **Querría** una habitación.（我想要一間房）—— 客氣

第四個是**把不規則字根用回原形**：

- ✗ podería → ✓ **podría**
- ✗ teneríamos → ✓ **tendríamos**

未來式縮短的那十二個字根，條件式也一樣縮短。

> 實務建議：在店裡、餐廳、櫃台，把 ¿Puede...? 換成 ¿Podría...?，把 Quiero 換成 Querría 或 Me gustaría。這一個小改動就能讓整句話的語氣完全不同。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **dropping the accent**:

- ✗ podria → ✓ **podría**
- ✗ gustaria → ✓ **gustaría**

> Self-check: **all five** conditional forms carry an accent, without exception. That’s the mirror image of the future, where only nosotros goes without.

Second, **confusing it with the imperfect’s -ía**:

- **comía** = I was eating (imperfect, stem com-)
- **comería** = I would eat (conditional, stem is the whole infinitive comer)

The stem is the tell: the conditional keeps the full infinitive, the imperfect chops the ending off.

Third, **using the present where politeness is called for**. Grammatically fine, but the tone is very different:

- Quiero una habitación. (I want a room) — blunt
- **Querría** una habitación. (I’d like a room) — polite

Fourth, **restoring the full stem on the irregulars**:

- ✗ podería → ✓ **podría**
- ✗ teneríamos → ✓ **tendríamos**

The twelve stems that shorten in the future shorten here too.

> Practical advice: in shops, restaurants and at counters, swap ¿Puede…? for ¿Podría…?, and Quiero for Querría or Me gustaría. That one small change transforms the tone of the whole sentence.

title.zh: 否定命令式：代名詞會換位置

intro.zh:
肯定命令式（A1 學過）把代名詞黏在動詞後面。**否定命令式剛好相反** —— 代名詞回到動詞前面，而且動詞形式也不一樣。

否定命令式的形式跟 **usted 的命令式**同一套，只是 tú 那格要加 -s。

這一課的重點就是這個位置的翻轉：**肯定黏後面，否定放前面**。
intro.en:
Affirmative commands (from A1) attach the pronoun to the end of the verb. **Negative commands do the opposite** — the pronoun goes back in front, and the verb form changes too.

Negative commands use the same forms as the **usted imperative**, with an -s added for tú.

That positional flip is the heart of this lesson: **affirmative attaches, negative precedes.**

rule.zh: 否定命令式：**no + 動詞**（-ar → -e／-es，-er／-ir → -a／-as）。
rule.en: Negative command: **no + verb** (-ar → -e/-es, -er/-ir → -a/-as).

rule.zh: **代名詞放在 no 和動詞之間**，不再黏在動詞後面。
rule.en: The **pronoun goes between no and the verb**, no longer attached to the end.

gloss.zh: 把它給他。→ 別把它給他。
gloss.en: Give it to him. → Don’t give it to him.

rule.zh: **位置換了，重音符號就不需要了**。代名詞不再黏上去，音節數沒變。
rule.en: With the pronoun moved, **the written accent is no longer needed** — nothing was attached, so the syllable count is unchanged.

note.zh: 肯定要重音符號，否定不用
note.en: The affirmative needs the accent; the negative doesn’t.

rule.zh: 八個不規則的 tú 命令式**只影響肯定形式**，否定形式照規則走。
rule.en: The eight irregular tú imperatives **only affect the affirmative**; the negatives are regular.

examples.es: Haz la tarea. → No hagas eso.

gloss.en: Do the homework. → Don’t do that.

gloss.zh: 跟我說。→ 別跟我說那個。
gloss.en: Tell me. → Don’t tell me that.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**在否定句裡還把代名詞黏在後面**：

- ✗ No dígame. → ✓ **No me diga**.
- ✗ No cómprelo. → ✓ **No lo compre**.

> 自我檢查：句子裡有 no，代名詞就一定在動詞左邊。看到 no 後面接一個黏著代名詞的長字，就是位置錯了。

第二個是**否定形式沿用了肯定的動詞形狀**：

- ✗ No habla tan rápido.（habla 是肯定的 tú 命令式）→ ✓ No **hables** tan rápido.
- ✗ No come eso. → ✓ No **comas** eso.

否定的 tú 命令式要用 -es／-as，不是肯定那一套。

第三個是**否定形式還留著重音符號**：

- ✗ No me ayúde. → ✓ No me **ayude**.

重音符號原本是為了黏上代名詞才補的。代名詞移走了，符號也跟著走。

第四個是**以為不規則的 tú 命令式在否定句也不規則**：

- ✗ No ten miedo. → ✓ No **tengas** miedo.
- ✗ No haz eso. → ✓ No **hagas** eso.

ten、haz、di、ven 這些只有肯定形式是不規則的。

> 記憶策略：肯定和否定是**鏡像** —— 肯定「動詞 + 代名詞」黏成一個字並補重音；否定「no + 代名詞 + 動詞」三個分開的字，不用重音。想清楚是哪一邊，位置自然就對了。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **still attaching the pronoun in a negative command**:

- ✗ No dígame. → ✓ **No me diga**.
- ✗ No cómprelo. → ✓ **No lo compre**.

> Self-check: if the sentence has no, the pronoun is to the left of the verb. A long word with a pronoun glued on sitting right after no means the position is wrong.

Second, **keeping the affirmative verb form in the negative**:

- ✗ No habla tan rápido. (habla is the affirmative tú command) → ✓ No **hables** tan rápido.
- ✗ No come eso. → ✓ No **comas** eso.

Negative tú commands take -es/-as, not the affirmative set.

Third, **keeping the written accent in the negative**:

- ✗ No me ayúde. → ✓ No me **ayude**.

The accent existed only because a pronoun had been attached. Move the pronoun and the accent goes with it.

Fourth, **assuming the irregular tú commands stay irregular when negated**:

- ✗ No ten miedo. → ✓ No **tengas** miedo.
- ✗ No haz eso. → ✓ No **hagas** eso.

ten, haz, di and ven are irregular in the affirmative only.

> A strategy: the two are **mirror images** — affirmative is “verb + pronoun”, one word with an accent; negative is “no + pronoun + verb”, three separate words with no accent. Decide which side you’re on and the position follows.

title.zh: por 與 para：兩個都翻成「為了」
title.en: por and para: two words, one translation

intro.zh:
por 和 para 常常都被翻成「為了」「因為」，但它們在西班牙文裡分工很清楚。

最好用的一個判準：

- **para 指向終點** —— 目的、對象、期限、方向。往前看。
- **por 指向原因與過程** —— 理由、經過、交換、時間長度。往回看或看中間。

這一課把常見的用法各自列出來，並用同一組句子做對比。
intro.en:
por and para often land on the same English words — “for”, “because of” — but in Spanish their jobs are clearly divided.

The most useful single test:

- **para points at a destination** — a purpose, a recipient, a deadline, a direction. It looks forward.
- **por points at causes and processes** — a reason, a route, an exchange, a duration. It looks back, or at the middle.

This lesson lists the common uses of each and then contrasts them on the same sentences.

rule.zh: **para**：目的（後面接不定式）、對象、期限、方向。
rule.en: **para**: purpose (followed by an infinitive), recipient, deadline, destination.

gloss.zh: 我學西班牙文是為了旅行。
gloss.en: I study Spanish in order to travel.

examples.es: La tarea es para el lunes.

rule.zh: **por**：原因、經過的路徑、交換、時間長度、一天當中的時段。
rule.en: **por**: cause, route travelled through, exchange, duration, part of the day.

gloss.en: We didn’t go out because of the rain.
We walked through the historic centre.
I bought it for twenty dollars.

examples.es: Estuve en Cuenca por tres días.

gloss.en: I was in Cuenca for three days.

rule.zh: **同一句換一個字，意思就變了。**
rule.en: **Swap one word in the same sentence and the meaning changes.**

gloss.zh: 我是因為你才做的。（你是原因）
gloss.en: I did it because of you.

gloss.zh: 我做這個是要給你的。（你是對象）

gloss.en: I go out through the door.

gloss.zh: 我出發去辦公室。（目的地）
gloss.en: I set off for the office.

rule.zh: 幾個**固定搭配**直接記起來，不用推。
rule.en: A few **fixed expressions** are simply learned as they are.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**用 para 講原因**：

- ✗ No salimos para la lluvia. → ✓ No salimos **por** la lluvia.

> 自我檢查：問「這是**原因**還是**目的**？」下雨是已經存在的原因，用 por。想達成的結果是目的，用 para。

第二個是**目的後面接了名詞而不是不定式**：

- ✗ Estudio para el viaje.（文法可以，但意思變成「為了那趟旅行而讀」）
- ✓ Estudio **para viajar**.（為了去旅行而讀）

para 講目的時，後面最自然的是不定式。

第三個是**時間長度用了 para**：

- ✗ Estuve en Cuenca para tres días. → ✓ Estuve en Cuenca **por** tres días.

持續多久是 por；「到什麼時候為止」才是 para。

第四個是**把 ¿Por qué? 和 ¿Para qué? 當成同一句**：

- **¿Por qué estudias español?** 你為什麼學西班牙文？（問原因）
- **¿Para qué estudias español?** 你學西班牙文要幹嘛？（問目的）

> 記憶策略：把 para 想成一支箭指向終點（目的、對象、期限、目的地），把 por 想成一條穿過中間的線（原因、路徑、交換、期間）。分不出來的時候，先問「這是終點，還是過程？」
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **using para for a cause**:

- ✗ No salimos para la lluvia. → ✓ No salimos **por** la lluvia.

> Self-check: ask “is this a **cause** or a **goal**?” The rain is a cause that already exists, so por. A result you are aiming at is a goal, so para.

Second, **following a purpose with a noun instead of an infinitive**:

- ✗ Estudio para el viaje. (grammatical, but it means “I study for the sake of that trip”)
- ✓ Estudio **para viajar**. (I study in order to travel)

When para expresses purpose, an infinitive is the natural continuation.

Third, **using para for duration**:

- ✗ Estuve en Cuenca para tres días. → ✓ Estuve en Cuenca **por** tres días.

How long something lasted is por; a cut-off point is para.

Fourth, **treating ¿Por qué? and ¿Para qué? as the same question**:

- **¿Por qué estudias español?** Why do you study Spanish? (asking the reason)
- **¿Para qué estudias español?** What are you studying Spanish for? (asking the goal)

> A strategy: picture para as an arrow pointing at an endpoint (purpose, recipient, deadline, destination), and por as a line running through the middle (cause, route, exchange, duration). When stuck, ask “is this the endpoint, or the process?”

title.zh: 關係代名詞：把兩句話接成一句
title.en: Relative pronouns: joining two sentences into one

intro.zh:
關係代名詞用來把兩句話接起來，避免重複同一個名詞。

最常用的只有幾個：

- **que** —— 涵蓋範圍最廣，人和東西都可以用
- **quien / quienes** —— 只用於人，通常跟在介系詞後面
- **donde** —— 地點
- **lo que** —— 指前面整件事，不是某個名詞

重點是：**que 不能省略**。
intro.en:
Relative pronouns join two sentences so you don’t repeat the same noun.

Only a handful come up often:

- **que** — the broadest, used for both people and things
- **quien / quienes** — people only, usually after a preposition
- **donde** — places
- **lo que** — refers to a whole idea rather than one noun

The key point: **que can never be dropped.**

rule.zh: **que** 是最常用的，人和東西都能接。
rule.en: **que** is the workhorse, used for both people and things.

rule.en: **quien / quienes** are for people only, and appear most often after a preposition.

rule.en: **donde** is used for places, replacing phrases like en el que.

rule.en: **lo que** refers to the whole preceding idea, not to a single noun.

rule.zh: **que 不能省略。**句子少了它會直接不成立。
rule.en: **que can’t be dropped.** Without it the sentence simply falls apart.

examples.es: El libro que compré es bueno.

gloss.en: The book I bought is good.

examples.es: La sopa que pedí está fría.

gloss.en: The soup I ordered is cold.

pitfalls.zh:
最容易犯的錯是**把 que 省略掉**：

- ✗ El libro compré es bueno. → ✓ El libro **que** compré es bueno.
- ✗ La sopa pedí está fría. → ✓ La sopa **que** pedí está fría.

> 自我檢查：兩個動詞（compré 和 es）之間一定要有東西把它們接起來。少了 que，兩個子句就直接撞在一起了。

第二個是**在該用 que 的地方用了 quien**：

- ✗ La chica quien trabaja aquí… → ✓ La chica **que** trabaja aquí…

quien 主要出現在**介系詞後面**（con quien、a quien、de quien）。沒有介系詞的時候，用 que 就好，即使指的是人。

第三個是**lo que 和 que 混用**：

- **el libro que compré**（que 指的是「書」這個名詞）
- **lo que compré**（lo que 指的是「我買的東西」，沒有具體名詞）

判準：前面有沒有一個具體的名詞可以指？有就用 que，沒有就用 lo que。

第四個是**地點用了 que 但少了介系詞**：

- ✗ El restaurante que comimos… → ✓ El restaurante **donde** comimos…（或 en el que comimos）

> 記憶策略：先把兩個短句分開想 —— 「我買了那本書」＋「那本書很好」。找出重複的名詞，用 que 把它接起來，重複的那個就不用再說一次了。
pitfalls.en:
The most common mistake is **dropping que**:

- ✗ El libro compré es bueno. → ✓ El libro **que** compré es bueno.
- ✗ La sopa pedí está fría. → ✓ La sopa **que** pedí está fría.

> Self-check: something has to join the two verbs (compré and es). Without que, the two clauses just collide.

Second, **using quien where que belongs**:

- ✗ La chica quien trabaja aquí… → ✓ La chica **que** trabaja aquí…

quien mainly appears **after a preposition** (con quien, a quien, de quien). With no preposition, use que — even for people.

Third, **mixing up lo que and que**:

- **el libro que compré** (que points at the noun “book”)
- **lo que compré** (lo que means “the thing I bought”, with no noun stated)

The test: is there a specific noun to point at? If yes, que; if not, lo que.

Fourth, **using que for a place without a preposition**:

- ✗ El restaurante que comimos… → ✓ El restaurante **donde** comimos… (or en el que comimos)

> A strategy: think of the two short sentences separately — “I bought the book” + “the book is good”. Find the repeated noun, join them with que, and drop the second mention.

explain.zh: -a 結尾不保證陰性，-o 結尾也不保證陽性：problema、idioma、clima、mapa 是陽性，cama、sopa 是陰性，mano、foto 反過來。關係代名詞 el que／la que 要跟先行詞一致，所以這裡選錯，後面整句都會錯。
explain.en: An -a ending does not guarantee feminine, nor an -o ending masculine: problema, idioma, clima and mapa are masculine, cama and sopa are feminine, and mano and foto go the other way. The relative el que / la que agrees with the noun it points back to, so getting this wrong derails the rest of the sentence.
